title: Stationary Drop Punt
objective: Develop a technically sound stationary drop punt by teaching correct ball drop, body position, foot contact and follow-through before introducing movement or defensive pressure.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Spread pairs evenly across the training area to prevent footballs crossing into neighbouring groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football.
Player A performs a stationary drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets before returning the kick.
Continue for the nominated time.
Swap the preferred kicking foot after several minutes if appropriate.
Players should prioritise correct technique rather than kicking distance.
coachingPoints: Guide the ball onto the boot rather than throwing it.
Keep their head over the football.
Strike the ball with the laces of the boot.
Follow through directly towards the target.
Encourage smooth, controlled kicking rather than maximum power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Provide one coaching correction before allowing several repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Throwing the ball onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football gently from the hands.
Keep the chest over the football.
Finish balanced on the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Looking at the target too early
commonErrors.correction: Watch the football until contact.
Finish with the kicking leg pointing towards the target.

regressions: Allow players to stop and reset after every kick.
Slow the pace of the activity.
Demonstrate the technique again before restarting.
successIndicators: Maintain balance throughout the kicking action.
matchApplication:
The drop punt is the primary kicking technique used throughout Australian Football.
This drill develops the technical foundation required for:
Maintaining possession.
Passing to teammates.
Kicking inside 50.
Defensive exits.
Goal kicking.
General field kicking.
Every advanced kicking drill in the AFCRL builds upon the skills developed in KK-001.

title: Partner Accuracy Challenge
objective: Develop the ability to consistently deliver the football to a teammate's advantage by improving kicking accuracy, control and judgement of kicking weight. Players learn that an effective pass is one that allows the receiver to mark or gather the football with minimal movement.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Each pair should have sufficient space to kick safely without interfering with neighbouring groups.
The receiving player should remain stationary throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B.
The objective is to deliver the football directly to Player B's chest without requiring them to move their feet.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B immediately returns the kick using the same objective.
Continue for the allocated time.
Coaches may introduce a simple scoring system:
2 points for a chest mark.
1 point if the receiver gathers the football cleanly after one bounce.
0 points if the receiver must move significantly or the football misses the target.
The emphasis should remain on quality rather than competition.
coachingPoints: Look at the target before beginning the kicking action.
Kick to where the receiver can comfortably mark the football.
Match the force of the kick to the required distance.
Maintain the same drop punt technique regardless of distance.
Stay balanced throughout the kicking action.
Players should understand that kicking accurately is more important than kicking hard.
coachingCues: "Kick to your teammate, not at them."
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver is forced to move.
Encourage players to evaluate each kick before receiving coaching feedback.

commonErrors.correction: Finish directly towards the target.
Reduce the height of the ball drop and maintain a flatter trajectory.
Reduce leg speed and focus on control.
Complete the follow-through and accelerate through the football.
Encourage the kicker to visualise the exact landing point before kicking.

regressions: Encourage players to stop and reset after each kick.
successIndicators: Deliver the football directly to the receiver.
Require minimal movement from the receiver.
Demonstrate good judgement of kicking weight.
Improve accuracy over the duration of the drill.
matchApplication: Most possessions in Australian Football involve passing to a teammate under little or no pressure. This drill develops the fundamental ability to consistently hit a teammate's preferred side, allowing the next possession to be completed quickly and efficiently.

title: Kick and Follow
objective: Teach players to move immediately after disposing of the football rather than remaining stationary. Players kick to a teammate, follow their kick and rotate continuously through the drill.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 15 m per group
setup:
Create two lines facing each other.
Place one cone at the front of each line.
Recommended distance between lines:
Under 8–10: 10 metres.
Under 12–14: 15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 20 metres.
Place a second cone approximately three metres behind each front cone to organise the waiting players.
The football begins with the first player in one line.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B at the opposite line.
Player A immediately follows the kick by running to the back of Player B’s line.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets and kicks to the next player in the opposite line.
Player B follows the kick to the back of that line.
The drill continues in a continuous pattern.
Players should communicate the intended target before kicking.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football before reaching the kicking point.
Kick accurately to the receiver’s advantage.
Run past the receiver rather than stopping in the middle.
Maintain appropriate spacing in the lines.
The drill should flow continuously without players standing in the kicking lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Players crossing through the kicking lane.
If lines become long, create additional groups.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the kick and remains stationary
commonErrors.correction: Run immediately after the football leaves the boot.
Follow the kick outside the main kicking lane.
Demand early voice and eye contact.
Require players to balance before kicking.
Divide players into smaller groups.

progressions: Require players to use the non-preferred foot.
Add a short lead before receiving.
Add a handball before the kick.
regressions: Allow players to walk after kicking.
Remove the follow run until kicking accuracy improves.
Use a stationary partner drill first.
matchApplication:
Players must continue working after disposal during a match.
Following the football can create:
A handball receive.
An overlap.
Support at the next contest.
Defensive cover if possession is lost.

title: Moving Target Kicking
objective: Teach players to kick accurately to a teammate who is moving rather than standing still. Players learn to place the football into the receiver’s running path so they can mark without slowing down or changing direction.
setup:
Create two lines facing each other approximately 20 metres apart.
Place a starting cone five metres to the side of each receiving line.
The first receiver starts at the side cone rather than directly in front of the kicker.
The football begins with the first player in the opposite line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins at the side cone.
The receiver leads diagonally into the space between the two lines.
The kicker waits until the receiver begins moving.
The kicker delivers the football in front of the receiver.
The receiver marks while continuing forward.
The receiver carries the football to the opposite line.
The kicker moves to the receiving line.
The drill repeats in the opposite direction.
The lead should begin before the kick is released.
coachingPoints: Kick to where the receiver is going.
Place the football slightly in front of the receiver.
Match the weight of the kick to the speed of the lead.
Avoid kicking directly at the receiver’s current position.
The receiver should accelerate into the football rather than waiting underneath it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing between the lead and kick.

commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the receiver’s running path.
Wait until the kicker is balanced and ready.
Kick flatter and further in front.

commonErrors.error: Kicker watches the football instead of the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Scan the receiver before beginning the kicking action.
Require the receiver to call before leading.

progressions: Increase the speed of the lead.
Add a passive defender following the receiver.
regressions: Allow the receiver to walk through the pattern.
Stop and reset after each repetition.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Time the kick with the lead.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
matchApplication:
Players regularly kick to teammates who are leading into space.
Accurate placement allows the receiver to:
Mark without slowing down.
Play on quickly.
Maintain attacking momentum.
Avoid nearby defenders.

title: Short Approach Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt from a Short Approach
objective: Progress players from stationary kicking to executing a drop punt after a short, controlled approach. Players learn to coordinate their steps, ball preparation and kicking action without rushing.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 20 m
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Place a starting cone approximately three metres behind each player’s kicking cone.
Recommended kicking distances:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres.
Under 12–14: 12–15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres.
Players begin at the rear starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football at the starting cone.
Player A walks or jogs forward for two to four controlled steps.
Player A performs a drop punt from the kicking cone.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets at their starting cone.
Player B repeats the short approach and kick.
Continue for the allocated time.
Increase approach speed only when technique remains consistent.
The approach should remain controlled rather than becoming a sprint.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football during the approach.
Guide the football onto the boot.
Avoid taking an excessively long final step.
Continue moving naturally after the kick.
The kicking action should remain similar to the stationary drop punt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes as speed increases.
Reduce the approach speed if technique deteriorates.

commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and regain control.
Position the football before the final two steps.
Shorten the final step to keep the body balanced.
Maintain smooth forward momentum through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop moves across the body
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football directly over the kicking foot.

progressions: Progress to a continuous running kick.
Receive a handball before beginning the approach.
regressions: Allow players to rehearse the steps without the football.
successIndicators: Coordinate the approach and kicking action.
matchApplication:
Players rarely kick from a completely stationary position during general play.
This drill introduces the movement coordination required to prepare and execute the football while approaching the point of disposal.

title: Ground Ball Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball cleanly, accelerate away from the contest and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to secure possession before transitioning quickly into the kicking action.
players: Minimum: 4 Ideal: 8–16 Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
setup:
Create a straight lane.
Place:
A starting cone.
A ground-ball cone five to eight metres ahead.
A kicking cone another five to eight metres ahead.
A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
A feeder stands beside the ground-ball cone.
Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A runs from the starting cone.
The feeder rolls the football into Player A’s path.
Player A lowers the body and gathers the football cleanly.
Player A accelerates away from the collection point.
Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
Player A executes a running drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player A continues to the receiving line.
Player B returns to the starting line with the football.
Rotate the feeder regularly.
The ground ball should be rolled at a realistic but controllable speed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with controlled speed.
Lower the hips and keep the head over the ball.
Gather the football cleanly before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Players should not attempt to kick before possession is secure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: If players repeatedly fumble, reduce the speed of the rolled football.

commonErrors.error: Player bends only at the waist
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bend the knees.
Gather with two hands whenever space allows.

commonErrors.error: Player looks towards the target before securing the football
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection before lifting the eyes.
Accelerate first, then move the football into kicking position.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while leaning forward excessively
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance during the steps after the gather.

progressions: Increase the speed or angle of the ground ball.
Require the player to change direction after gathering.
Begin with a contested ground ball.
regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
Remove the kicking component until collection improves.
successIndicators: Complete the sequence without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication:
Ground balls regularly begin attacking possessions.
Players must collect cleanly, escape immediate pressure and deliver accurately to a teammate.
This drill applies to:
Loose-ball wins.
Crumbing.
Contested-ball exits.
Defensive rebounds.
Midfield stoppage releases.

title: Contested Gather and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to win or secure a contested ground ball, escape pressure and execute an effective kick. Players learn to place the body between the opponent and the football before creating enough space to dispose accurately.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Create:
A feeder position.
A contest area approximately six metres wide.
Two exit gates beyond the contest.
One kicking target 20–30 metres ahead.
Two players begin on opposite sides of the contest area.
The feeder stands five to ten metres away with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls or bounces the football into the contest area.
Both players compete to gain possession.
The player who wins the football protects it and exits through either gate.
The opposing player applies controlled pressure without completing a full tackle.
The ball winner accelerates into space.
The ball winner kicks to the target.
Players reset and rotate.
Alternate opponents regularly.
The drill ends if the football becomes trapped for an extended period. Restart with a new feed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with the body low.
Position the body between the opponent and the football.
Gather with two hands when possible.
The first objective is to secure possession. The second is to create space for the kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Stop the drill if contact becomes uncontrolled.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches without using the body
commonErrors.correction: Win position between the opponent and football first.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright at the contest
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and keep the feet moving.

commonErrors.error: Ball winner tries to kick immediately
commonErrors.correction: Exit pressure before preparing the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Player runs directly into the opponent
commonErrors.correction: Use the open gate away from pressure.
Regain balance after the exit before kicking.

progressions: Require a handball receive before kicking.
Reduce the size of the exit gates.
Allow full tackling for appropriately prepared groups.
regressions: Roll the football directly towards one player.
Allow the ball winner to stop after exiting.
successIndicators: Recover quickly after losing the contest.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates possessions that begin with:
A loose ball.
A stoppage spill.
A marking contest.
A defensive ground ball.
A forward-half turnover.
Players must secure possession before creating a usable disposal.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Time-Limited Kick
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select a target and execute an accurate kick within a limited period. Players learn to prepare before possession and avoid wasting time once the football is secured.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one central receiving cone.
Position three targets approximately 20 metres away at different angles.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres from the central receiver.
Players form lines at the feeder, receiver and target positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the target positions.
The feeder passes the football to the receiver.
As the football arrives, the coach begins a countdown.
The receiver must select and kick to a target within the allowed time.
Recommended time limits:
Under 12: Four seconds.
Under 14: Three seconds.
Under 16 and above: Two to three seconds.
The selected target marks or gathers the football.
Players rotate positions.
Continue for the allocated time.
The coach may nominate that one target is unavailable immediately before possession.
coachingPoints: The time limit should challenge decision speed without making accurate execution impossible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Adjust the countdown to match player ability.

commonErrors.error: Player waits until possession to scan
commonErrors.correction: Identify targets before the football arrives.
Keep the technique controlled despite the countdown.

commonErrors.error: Player searches for the perfect option
commonErrors.correction: Use the first safe and effective target.
Prepare the football immediately after possession.
Add one second until players regain confidence.

progressions: Remove one option on the coach’s call.
Require the non-preferred foot for selected targets.
Begin with a ground ball gather.
regressions: Allow the receiver to begin with the football.
matchApplication:
Players often have limited time after:
Taking possession in traffic.
Receiving at half-back.
Winning a clearance.
Marking and playing on.
Collecting a loose football.

title: Forward Entry After Ground Ball
primarySkill: Forward Entry After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to gather a loose football outside forward 50 and quickly convert possession into an effective forward entry. Players learn to secure the football first, accelerate from the contest and identify the best attacking option.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place:
One starting cone 55 metres from goal.
One ground-ball collection zone eight metres ahead.
Three forward starting positions inside 50.
One feeder beside the collection zone.
Players form lines at the starting and forward positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker runs towards the collection zone.
The feeder rolls the football into the attacker’s path.
The attacker gathers cleanly.
The attacker accelerates away from the collection point.
The forwards begin their leads.
The attacker scans and selects the best option.
The attacker delivers inside 50.
The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all positions.
Vary the ground-ball angle and forward leads.
The player should not look forward before securing possession.
coachingPoints: Get low and use two hands.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Lift the eyes early after the gather.
Prepare the football during the run.
Select the forward with the best space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes immediately after gathering.

commonErrors.error: Player looks forward before securing the ball
commonErrors.correction: Complete the gather first.

commonErrors.error: Attacker remains low for too long
commonErrors.correction: Rise and accelerate after possession is secure.
Move it into kicking position during the exit steps.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks to the first voice heard
commonErrors.correction: Scan all forward options.

commonErrors.error: Technique collapses after a poor gather
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance before disposal.

regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Win a loose ball outside forward 50.
Gather a spill from a contest.
Recover a turnover.
Crumb a marking contest.
Attack before the opposition can reset.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Forward Entry from Opposite Foot
objective: Develop the ability to deliver inside 50 using the non-preferred foot when body position, pressure or field location removes the preferred-side option.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
Create two leading targets positioned so the non-preferred foot provides the more natural kicking angle.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres behind or beside the ball carrier.
Players rotate through feeder, kicker and forward roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker receives from the feeder.
The forwards begin their leads.
The kicker must use the non-preferred foot.
The kicker selects the better of the two targets.
The kicker delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate positions.
Repeat from both sides of the ground.
Keep the distance realistic enough for sound technique.
coachingPoints: Hold the football correctly for the non-preferred side.
Guide it directly over the kicking foot.
Select a target within realistic range.
Avoid turning back onto the preferred foot automatically.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Willingness to use the non-preferred foot.
Whether players turn back into pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player turns back onto the preferred foot
commonErrors.correction: Commit to the non-preferred-side option.
Hold and guide it directly over the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Player tries to kick too far
commonErrors.correction: Choose a closer target and prioritise contact.
Slow the approach and finish balanced.

commonErrors.error: Decision is delayed through lack of confidence
commonErrors.correction: Scan early and commit once the option appears.

progressions: Add passive pressure on the preferred side.
regressions: Return to basic non-preferred foot kicking.
matchApplication:
Non-preferred foot forward entries are required when:
Opponents block the preferred side.
Players receive near the boundary.
Body position limits turning.
Fast ball movement demands immediate disposal.
A teammate is open on the opposite angle.

title: Forward Entry Decision Game
objective: Develop live forward-entry decisions in a constrained game. Players learn to select between leading targets, space, short possession and deeper options while defenders actively influence the available lanes.
players: Minimum: 12 Ideal: 16–24 Maximum: 30 using two areas
setup:
Create a playing area extending from approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line.
Divide players into:
Attacking team.
Defending team.
Optional neutral transition players.
Recommended starting format:
Four to six attackers.
Three to five defenders.
One or two neutral players outside forward 50.
Start each repetition with a neutral player or coach feeding the football to an attacker outside 50.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession outside forward 50.
Forwards create leads and maintain spacing.
Defenders attempt to deny the most dangerous options.
The ball carrier decides whether to:
Kick to a leading forward.
Kick into space.
Use a short possession.
Switch the angle.
Retain the football.
The attack continues until:
A shot at goal is completed.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.
Reset and begin a new repetition.
Rotate attackers and defenders regularly.
Award points for decision quality as well as scoring.
Optional scoring:
Three points for a marked kick that creates a shot.
Two points for a forward gathering a kick to advantage.
One point for retaining possession inside 50.
Bonus point for using a non-preferred foot successfully.
coachingPoints: Avoid leading into the same area.
Avoid low-percentage kicks to outnumbered contests.
Retain possession when no strong entry exists.
The coach should avoid stopping every repetition. Allow players to experience the consequences of their decisions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain possession when required.
Use brief feedback between repetitions rather than constant interruption.

commonErrors.correction: Maintain separate leading lanes and depth.
Scan short, lateral and space options.

commonErrors.error: Attackers hold the football too long
commonErrors.correction: Use the first strong option before defenders recover.
Retain possession or change the angle.
Kick to the forward’s protected side or into open space.

progressions: Add transition after a defensive turnover.
Restrict the number of possessions before entry.
Track entry type and scoring outcome.
regressions: Stop after the first forward entry.
matchApplication:
This drill directly replicates live inside-50 decision making, including:
Fast entries.
Slow entries.
Boundary entries.
Corridor entries.
Kicks to space.
Short possession.
Deep contests.
Entries under pressure.

title: Intercept and Switch
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute a switch immediately after winning an intercept possession. Players learn to use the opposition’s movement towards one side to access space on the opposite side.
setup:
Place:
One feeder on a boundary side.
One intended attacking target.
One intercept player between them.
One short release target centrally.
One wide switch target on the opposite side.
One forward outlet beyond the switch target.
Add one or two recovering defenders.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks towards the intended target.
The intercept player marks or wins possession.
The short release and switch target move immediately.
The interceptor may:
Kick directly to the switch.
Use the short release before switching.
The football moves to the opposite side.
The switch target delivers to the forward outlet.
Recovering defenders attempt to close the switch lanes.
Players rotate through all positions.
Repeat from both sides.
The intercept player must decide whether the direct switch is safe.
coachingPoints: Scan the opposite side before completing the intercept.
Recognise where the opposition has shifted.
Use a short release when the direct switch is too difficult.
Kick with appropriate distance and trajectory.
Avoid floating the football across the ground.
coachingCues: “Win it and see the far side.”
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Accuracy of the final outlet kick.

commonErrors.error: Interceptor automatically kicks down the same side
commonErrors.correction: Scan the opposite side immediately.

commonErrors.error: Direct switch is attempted through pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use the short release first.
Hold width until the kick is released.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick hangs in the air
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter trajectory when possible.
Prepare the next option before receiving.

progressions: Require a long non-preferred foot kick.
Continue into a live forward entry.
regressions: Allow the interceptor to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Choose direct or assisted switch appropriately.
matchApplication:
This drill develops the ability to exploit opposition shape after:
An intercept mark.
A turnover near the boundary.
A defensive spoil.
A pressured forward entry.
A loose-ball win at half-back.

title: Kick-In Decision Game
objective: Develop live kick-in decisions against an organised defensive structure. Players learn to select between short possession, switching play, playing on and kicking long according to the available space.
groundSize:
Defensive half of the ground
Approximately 80 m × full or reduced width
equipment: Bibs for attacking and defending teams.
setup:
Use the defensive half of the ground.
Divide players into:
Kick-in attacking team.
Defending team.
Optional neutral players.
Place attackers in realistic positions:
Short pockets.
Central release.
Wide outlets.
High target.
Opposite-side switch.
Defenders set up in a zone or match-up structure.
howTheDrillWorks:
Every repetition begins with a kick-in.
The attacking team attempts to exit the defensive area.
The kicker may:
Use a short option.
Play on.
Switch.
Kick long.
Defenders attempt to intercept or force the football to a low-value area.
The repetition continues until:
The attacking team exits beyond the designated line.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.
Reset with another kick-in.
Rotate kickers and player roles.
Award points for successful exits and defensive turnovers.
Optional scoring:
Three points for a controlled corridor exit.
Two points for a marked wide exit.
One point for retaining possession beyond defensive 50.
Two points to defenders for an intercept and shot at goal.

commonErrors.error: Kicker decides before seeing the defence
commonErrors.correction: Scan after the defensive structure is set.
Maintain short, medium and long options.
Hold position to preserve the switch.

commonErrors.error: Team completes the first kick but provides no next option
commonErrors.correction: Support the receiver immediately.

commonErrors.error: Kicker repeatedly uses the same exit
commonErrors.correction: Base decisions on defender positioning.

regressions: Give the kicker one free short option.
matchApplication:
This drill directly replicates kick-in situations, including:
Short possession exits.
Long contests.
Switches.
Play-on kicks.
Corridor attacks.
Defensive turnovers.

title: Kick-In Chaos Exit
primarySkill: Decision Making in Broken Defensive Structures
objective: Train players to make effective kicking decisions when structures break down following a kick-in.
setup:
Begin with a normal kick-in.
The coach deliberately creates chaos by:
Calling random turnovers.
Sending extra defenders.
Holding players in zones.
Changing numerical advantages.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players must constantly solve changing situations while attempting to move the football cleanly from defence into attack.
Every repetition is different.

commonErrors.correction: Reset structure first.
Hold width.
Spread quickly.

successIndicators: Players quickly recover shape after unpredictable events.
matchApplication: Replicates broken play following kick-ins, turnovers and contested exits.

title: Full Ground Exit Pattern
objective: Develop complete team kicking patterns from defensive goal square to a shot on goal.
players:
Minimum: 18
Ideal: Full Squad
Maximum: Full Squad
setup:
Use full team positions.
Begin every repetition with:
Kick-in.
Intercept mark.
Ground-ball win.
Turnover.
howTheDrillWorks:
The team must execute its complete ball movement philosophy from defence through midfield and into a quality inside-50 entry before finishing with a shot on goal.
The coach scores:
Decision quality.
Ball movement.
Structure.
Scoring opportunity.
Execution.

commonErrors.correction: Re-establish width.
Retain possession.
Continue supporting.

successIndicators: The team consistently exits defence, transitions cleanly and creates high-quality scoring opportunities.
matchApplication: Replicates complete AFL team ball movement from defensive possession to goal.

title: Goal Square Chaos Finish
objective: Develop players' ability to score from unpredictable contests inside the goal square.
setup: The coach throws or kicks unpredictable footballs into a congested goal-square area where attackers and defenders compete.

commonErrors.correction: Shoot immediately when possible.
Stay composed in congestion.

matchApplication: Replicates real AFL goal-square chaos following spills, spoils and ground-ball contests.

title: Fatigue Set Shot
objective: Develop technical consistency immediately after repeated high-intensity efforts.
setup: Players complete repeated sprint efforts before taking a set shot.

commonErrors.correction: Take recovery breath.
Maintain posture.

matchApplication: Replicates fourth-quarter set shots.

title: Goal Kicking Circuit
objective: Develop complete goal-kicking versatility by rotating through multiple finishing scenarios.
setup:
Create six stations including:
Straight set shot.
Tight angle.
Snap.
Banana.
Running shot.
Ground-ball finish.
howTheDrillWorks: Players rotate continuously through every station before recording scores.

commonErrors.correction: Match technique to angle.
Reset each kick.

matchApplication: Replicates every common scoring opportunity.

title: Boundary Line Banana Challenge
objective: Develop confidence executing banana kicks from progressively tighter boundary-line positions.
setup: Mark five progressively tighter kicking locations along the boundary.
matchApplication: Replicates pocket finishes.

title: Around-the-Mark Specialist
primarySkill: Scoring Around the Player on the Mark
objective: Teach players to select the highest-percentage finish based on the position of the player on the mark.
setup:
Use movable cones representing different mark positions.
Players must decide:
Drop punt.
Snap.
Banana.
before every kick.
matchApplication: Improves tactical goal kicking.

title: Goal Kicking Decision Matrix
objective:
Develop decision making using the AFL goal-kicking matrix based on:
Distance.
Angle.
Pressure.
Dominant foot.
Players must verbalise why they selected:
Drop punt.
Snap.
Banana.
before executing.
matchApplication: Builds intelligent shot selection.

title: Complete Goal Kicking Assessment
relatedDrills: Used as the final assessment for the Goal Kicking module before progressing to Advanced Match Scenario Kicking (KK-101).

title: Corridor Kick Decision
objective: Develop the ability to recognise when to attack through the corridor and when to retain possession or switch play.
setup:
Mark a central corridor approximately 15 metres wide.
Play 5 v 5 or 6 v 6 with two wide channels.
Teams score bonus points for successfully using the corridor before entering the forward zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from half-back.
Teams progress the ball using kicks.
Players choose to:
Attack through the corridor.
Switch wide.
Retain possession.
If the corridor closes, players must immediately adapt.
Continue until a score or turnover.
coachingPoints: Support behind and ahead of the ball.

commonErrors.correction: Use width when required.
Scan earlier.
Move before the kick.

matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition through the corridor.

title: Corridor or Boundary Game
objective: Develop players' understanding of when the corridor is the highest-value option and when boundary football is the better tactical choice.
setup: Teams receive bonus points for making the correct tactical decision rather than simply scoring.
matchApplication: Improves tactical football intelligence.

title: Pressure Release Kick
primarySkill: Releasing Pressure with the Correct Kick
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute the best release kick while under immediate defensive pressure.
setup: Attackers begin trapped inside a confined area and must escape through accurate kicking.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive pressure exits.

title: High Press Escape
objective: Develop effective kicking solutions against aggressive opposition presses.
setup:
Defenders establish an AFL-style high press.
Attackers attempt multiple exit strategies.

title: Forward Half Retention
objective: Develop controlled possession inside attacking 50 before creating a high-quality scoring opportunity.
setup: Teams maintain possession inside forward 50 before attempting a score.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL forward-half possession football.

title: Elite Disposal Chain
objective: Develop elite AFL-level disposal chains through multiple phases.
setup: Teams complete predetermined and reactive kicking chains through defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition chains.

title: Advanced Match Scenario Rotation
primarySkill: Executing Kicks Across Multiple Match Scenarios
objective: Develop complete kicking adaptability by rotating through realistic AFL match scenarios.
setup:
Players rotate through ten scenarios including:
Defensive kick-in.
Corridor attack.
Boundary exit.
Intercept transition.
Forward entry.
Tight-angle goal.
Fatigue set shot.
Last-minute attack.
High press exit.
Broken-play recovery.

commonErrors.correction: React to what you see.
Scan earlier.
Talk continuously.

successIndicators: Transition effectively between phases of play.
matchApplication: Integrates every advanced kicking concept developed in KK-101 to KK-110 into realistic AFL match scenarios.

title: Defender Distribution Decision
objective: Develop key defenders' ability to identify and execute the highest-percentage distribution option after gaining possession. Players learn to scan the field before disposal, recognise opposition structure and choose between short, medium or long kicking options.
setup:
Position a key defender with the football inside defensive 50.
Create:
Two short options.
One central outlet.
One wide switch option.
One long boundary option.
Two defenders adjust their positions before every repetition to alter the available kicking lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
Coach signals play.
Defender scans all five options.
Defender selects the highest-percentage kick.
Ball movement continues for two additional disposals.
Reset with a different defensive structure.

commonErrors.correction: Read the defence first.
Take the safe outlet when required.
Scan the full field before disposal.

matchApplication: Replicates intercept marks, defensive rebounds and kick-ins.

title: Half-Back Quarterback
objective: Develop the distributor's ability to control tempo and launch attacking chains from half-back.
setup: The designated distributor receives repeated possessions from varying angles while teammates continually adjust their positioning.
matchApplication: Replicates elite AFL rebounding defenders.

title: Wing Link Kick
objective: Develop the winger's ability to connect defence and attack using intelligent positioning and accurate kicking.
setup: Create repeated transition chains between half-back, wing and half-forward.
matchApplication: Replicates elite AFL wing play.

title: Midfielder Exit Kick
objective: Develop midfielders' ability to deliver effective first kicks immediately after winning possession.
setup: Players begin with a simulated clearance before selecting the best kicking option.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL stoppage exits.

title: Midfielder Pressure Kick
objective: Develop composure while delivering accurate kicks despite immediate physical pressure.
setup: Players receive controlled body contact before disposing.
matchApplication: Replicates contested midfield football.

title: Inside Midfield Release
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute the release kick from heavy congestion.
setup: Small congested grid with outside support players.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL stoppage exits.

title: Outside Midfield Connection
objective: Develop outside midfielders' ability to receive, carry and distribute effectively.
setup: Continuous overlap kicking drill.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition running.

title: Forward Lead Delivery
objective: Develop precise delivery to leading forwards using the correct kicking weight and placement.
setup: Forwards lead from multiple starting positions while midfielders deliver.
coachingPoints: Keep the ball away from defenders.
matchApplication: Replicates inside-50 entries.

title: Forward Entry Distributor
objective: Develop half-forwards' ability to choose between shooting, centring or lowering the eyes inside forward 50.
setup: Multiple forward options are presented each repetition.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL attacking decision making.

title: Position-Specific Kicking Challenge
objective: Assess every player's ability to execute the kicking decisions required for their specific playing position.
setup:
Players rotate through five positional stations:
Key Defender
Half-Back Distributor
Wing
Midfielder
Forward
Each station contains unique decision-making challenges relevant to that position.

commonErrors.correction: Encourage scanning and varied solutions.
Reinforce positional objectives.
Slow decision-making and refocus on fundamentals.

successIndicators: Execute the correct decision for their position.
matchApplication: This assessment integrates every position-specific kicking skill from KK-111 to KK-120 and prepares players for advanced elite match simulation drills beginning with KK-121 – Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure.

title: Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure
primarySkill: Selecting and Executing the Best Kicking Option Under Pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to scan, assess risk and execute the highest-value kicking option while under immediate physical and time pressure.
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark three vertical kicking channels:
Boundary channel.
Central channel.
Opposite-side channel.
Position one target player at the end of each channel.
Assign different point values to each target based on difficulty and tactical value.
Begin each repetition with a contested possession or coach-fed football.
howTheDrillWorks:
A player wins or receives possession under defensive pressure.
The player has a limited period to scan and dispose of the football.
Teammates create short, medium and long options.
The player selects the most appropriate kick based on:
Defensive positioning.
Available space.
Teammate movement.
Turnover risk.
Play continues for three to five disposals.
A turnover immediately changes the direction of play.
Reset after a successful target connection, score or boundary exit.
coachingPoints: Identify pressure before looking for distance.
Use the safest attacking option rather than the most ambitious option.
Keep feet active while assessing the field.
Understand the consequences of central turnovers.
Balance speed of play with disposal quality.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Support movement around the ball carrier.

commonErrors.correction: Encourage scanning before possession arrives.
Require assessment of short and central options first.

commonErrors.error: Decision changes during the kicking action
commonErrors.correction: Make the decision earlier and commit fully.
Demand movement before the ball carrier gains possession.

commonErrors.error: Central kick is forced under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use width or retain possession when the corridor is closed.

progressions: Require alternating short and long options.
matchApplication: Replicates high-pressure possessions where players must make rapid kicking decisions through congestion, during transition or late in matches.

title: Final Two-Minute Attack
primarySkill: Rapid Ball Movement When Chasing a Score
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move the football rapidly and create a high-quality scoring opportunity when trailing late in a match.
setup:
The attacking team trails by four points with two minutes remaining.
Play begins from defensive 50.
The defending team sets up behind the football.
Players begin in realistic positional structures.
The attacking team must create a scoring opportunity before time expires.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession in defence.
Players must quickly decide whether to:
Attack through the corridor.
Use the wing and overlap.
Switch before accelerating.
Kick long to an isolated contest.
The countdown continues throughout the repetition.
The attacking team wins by scoring a goal.
The defending team wins by forcing a turnover, boundary stoppage or time expiry.
Teams rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Avoid repeated sideways possession when time is limited.
Create multiple scoring options rather than relying on one target.

commonErrors.correction: Encourage fast assessment before execution.
Attack forward once the defence is shifted.
Demand forward running immediately after disposal.
Lower the eyes and identify the best target.

commonErrors.error: Players lose track of the clock
commonErrors.correction: Assign continuous time communication.

progressions: Allow the defending team to flood deeper.
successIndicators: Move the ball quickly from defence.
Maintain support around the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Replicates late-game attacking situations where the team must score quickly from the back half.

title: Corridor Re-Entry Kick
primarySkill: Re-Entering the Corridor After Boundary Possession
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute the correct moment to move the football from the boundary back into the corridor.
setup:
Mark a boundary channel and a central corridor.
Begin possession in the boundary channel.
Position central attackers and defenders in the corridor.
Create two central entry gates.
The coach may open or close gates using coloured signals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team moves the football along the boundary.
Central players continually reposition to create an entry lane.
The ball carrier scans for the corridor option.
When the corridor becomes available, the player executes the re-entry kick.
The team accelerates forward following the central connection.
If the corridor remains closed, the team retains possession or continues along the boundary.
A turnover immediately reverses the direction of play.
coachingPoints: Avoid entering the corridor without forward support.
Wait until the central receiver has separation.
Move quickly after the central kick.
Maintain width until the corridor opportunity appears.
Recognise whether the defence is shifting or stationary.
Avoid telegraphing the kick too early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of transition after the kick.

commonErrors.error: Corridor kick is forced into congestion
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until separation appears.
Lead through the available window.

commonErrors.error: No forward support after central entry
commonErrors.correction: Push runners ahead before the kick.
Continue scanning and disguise the disposal.
Maintain boundary width until the moment of entry.

progressions: Reduce the width of the corridor.
Require a forward-50 entry after corridor connection.
Allow defenders to change structure during play.
successIndicators: Recognise the correct corridor entry moment.
Maintain structure before and after the kick.
matchApplication: Replicates switching from controlled boundary play into aggressive corridor transition.

title: Opposition Press Adaptation
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Strategy to Different Defensive Presses
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise different opposition defensive presses and adjust their kicking strategy without requiring direct instruction from the coach.
setup:
Prepare several defensive structures:
Full-ground press.
Half-ground press.
Boundary trap.
Corridor block.
Man-on-man defence.
Loose defender behind the ball.
The defending team changes its structure before or during each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession in defence.
The opposition establishes one of the nominated presses.
The attacking team must identify the structure without coach assistance.
Players select an appropriate exit strategy.
Play continues until the attacking team:
Reaches the wing.
Exits the defensive half.
Creates a forward entry.
A turnover allows the defending team to attack.
The defensive structure changes for the next repetition.
coachingPoints: Identify where the opposition has placed extra numbers.
Recognise which areas have been deliberately left open.
Avoid using the same exit pattern repeatedly.
Use short kicks to open long options.
Change tempo when the opposition adjusts.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Execution after the press is beaten.
Reaction when the first option closes.

commonErrors.correction: Read the opposition structure first.

commonErrors.error: Players attack the most heavily defended area
commonErrors.correction: Identify where the opposition has conceded space.
Move the football before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to communicate the press
commonErrors.correction: Nominate leaders to identify the structure aloud.

commonErrors.error: Team relaxes after beating the first line
commonErrors.correction: Continue attacking while the opposition is disorganised.

progressions: Change the defensive structure during the possession chain.
Prevent coaches from announcing the press.
Let the defending team design its own press.
regressions: Walk through each press before live play.
successIndicators: Adjust when the defensive structure changes.
matchApplication: Replicates preparing for and responding to different opposition defensive systems.

title: Elite Kicking Match Simulation
primarySkill: Applying the Complete Team Kicking System in Match Conditions
objective: Integrate all technical, tactical and position-specific kicking skills into a continuous match simulation with realistic pressure, scoring and coaching assessment.
setup:
Divide players into two match-balanced teams.
Use full positional structures.
Assign each team:
A defensive exit strategy.
A midfield transition strategy.
A forward-entry strategy.
A turnover-response strategy.
Set realistic match rules, interchange and scoring.
Prepare scenario cards that can be introduced during play.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins as a normal match simulation.
Coaches allow continuous play with minimal interruption.
Teams must apply their full kicking strategy.
At selected moments, the coach introduces scenarios such as:
Full opposition press.
Strong wind.
Wet football.
Final-two-minute situation.
Numerical disadvantage.
Spare defender.
Coaches assess both the decision and execution of each critical kick.
Teams review performance between blocks.
Play resumes with adjusted tactical objectives.
coachingPoints: Apply all kicking principles without relying on coach direction.
Protect the football in dangerous field positions.
Adapt to changing conditions and scenarios.

commonErrors.correction: Reinforce width, depth and positional connection.

commonErrors.error: Players rely on repeated long kicks
commonErrors.correction: Use possession and movement to create better options.
Balance attacking value against turnover risk.

commonErrors.error: Team slows after creating an advantage
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate before the opposition resets.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to adapt to new scenarios
commonErrors.correction: Reassess score, conditions, numbers and opposition structure.
Maintain leadership and role calls throughout.

progressions: Require teams to self-review between blocks.
successIndicators: Make appropriate decisions across the full ground.
Communicate and organise without coach direction.
matchApplication: Provides the closest training replication of competitive AFL kicking demands before formal match play.

title: Complete Kicking Competency Assessment
primarySkill: Comprehensive Assessment of AFL Kicking Competency
objective: Provide a complete assessment of each player’s kicking technique, versatility, decision making and tactical execution across every major AFL kicking situation.
groundSize: Full Ground with Multiple Assessment Stations
setup:
Create ten assessment stations:
Basic drop-punt technique.
Short-kick accuracy.
Medium and long kicking.
Preferred and non-preferred foot.
Kicking on the run.
Kicking under pressure.
Goal kicking.
Defensive exit decisions.
Forward-entry decisions.
Full-ground match simulation.
Prepare age-appropriate scoring standards for each station.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete each technical station.
Coaches record:
Accuracy.
Distance.
Trajectory.
Ball-drop consistency.
Balance.
Preferred and non-preferred-side performance.
Players then complete decision-making stations under pressure.
Goal-kicking performance is assessed from:
Set shots.
Running shots.
Snaps.
Bananas.
Tight angles.
Fatigue.
Players finish with a live match simulation.
Coaches combine all results into an individual kicking profile.
Each player receives priority development areas and recommended drills.
coachingPoints: Select the correct kick for the situation.
Maintain execution under pressure and fatigue.
Use both sides of the body.
Transfer isolated skills into match play.

commonErrors.error: Player focuses only on kicking distance
commonErrors.correction: Assess accuracy, trajectory and tactical value as well.
Reinforce consistent fundamentals.

commonErrors.error: Player performs well unopposed but struggles under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise pressure-based progression drills.
Include regular opposite-side development.

commonErrors.error: Decision making does not match technical ability
commonErrors.correction: Use scenario-based kicking drills.
Rebuild a repeatable routine.

commonErrors.error: Assessment results are treated as permanent
commonErrors.correction: Use results as a development baseline.

progressions: Compare results across multiple testing periods.
Use opposition pressure at every station.
Add match statistics to the assessment profile.
regressions: Assess one skill group per session.
Use larger targets for younger players.
successIndicators: Accurate short, medium and long disposal.
matchApplication: Provides a complete evidence-based profile of each player’s ability to execute AFL kicking skills in technical, tactical and match-pressure environments.

KK-041 to KK-060 – Ball Movement and Forward Entry
KK-061 to KK-080 – Possession and Transition Kicking
KK-101 to KK-120 – Advanced and Position-Specific Kicking
KK-121 to KK-149 – Elite Decision Making and Match Simulation
